project_name: The Man Who Would Be King
premise: Two seasoned vagabonds and former soldiers, weary of the constraints of British India, devise an audacious plan to travel to the uncharted region of Kafiristan and establish themselves as kings. A weary newspaperman, initially just a messenger, becomes their reluctant guide and chronicler as they prepare for their impossible quest.
logline: After a chance encounter on a train, two ambitious vagabonds recruit a cynical newspaperman to help them map and conquer the uncharted mountains of Kafiristan, setting in motion a tale of imperial ambition and brotherhood.
thematic_spine: The pursuit of grand ambition and self-invention inevitably collides with the harsh realities of human nature and the unforgiving world.
emotional_promise: A thrilling, atmospheric adventure exploring the heights of human ambition, the bonds of brotherhood, and the seductive danger of dreaming beyond one's station.
target_audience: Fans of classic adventure literature, historical fiction, and colonial-era tales

characters.name: The Narrator
characters.external_goal: Deliver a message for a stranger and fulfill his duties at the newspaper office.
characters.internal_need: To find purpose and escape the monotony of colonial bureaucracy.
characters.core_fear: Irrelevance and being trapped in a mundane existence.
characters.primary_strength: Observant, dutiful, and adaptable to harsh conditions.
characters.fatal_flaw: Passive and easily swept along by others' schemes.
characters.backstory: Travels extensively through Central India and the desert, eventually taking a job at a newspaper office.
characters.voice_notes: Reflective, slightly cynical, descriptive, and measured.
characters.change_axis: Transitions from a weary, passive observer to an active participant and reluctant enabler of grand ambition.
characters.contradictions: Cynical about empire yet fascinated by adventure; claims to want rest but engages in dangerous travel.
characters.continuity_facts: Travels Intermediate class, works at a newspaper, met the men on the Mhow train, delivers the message at Marwar Junction.

characters.name: Daniel Dravot
characters.external_goal: Conquer Kafiristan and establish himself as a king.
characters.internal_need: Recognition, power, and escape from obscurity.
characters.primary_strength: Charismatic, strategic, and experienced in military drilling.
characters.fatal_flaw: Hubris and overconfidence in his own abilities.
characters.backstory: Served with Roberts's Army, traveled extensively across India as a vagabond and correspondent.
characters.voice_notes: Confident, commanding, uses 'Dan', speaks with authority and conviction.
characters.change_axis: Evolves from a wandering vagabond to a determined, self-proclaimed monarch-in-waiting.
characters.contradictions: Claims strict discipline (Contrack) but pursues an insane, high-risk dream.
characters.secrets: Full strategic plan for subverting local kings and establishing a dynasty.
characters.values: Brotherhood, ambition, discipline, and loyalty to the Contrack.
characters.taboos: Drink and women (strictly forbidden by the Contrack).
characters.continuity_facts: Has a great red beard, described as a 'great swell', served in the army, travels with Carnehan.

characters.name: Peachey Carnehan
characters.external_goal: Accompany Dravot to Kafiristan and share in the glory of kingship.
characters.internal_need: Purpose, brotherhood, and escape from poverty.
characters.fatal_flaw: Gullibility and lack of strategic foresight compared to Dravot.
characters.backstory: Served in the army, traveled India with Dravot, worked various odd jobs.
characters.voice_notes: Pragmatic, slightly less eloquent, uses 'Peachey', speaks plainly.
characters.change_axis: Follows Dravot's lead, transitioning from a fellow vagabond to a committed conspirator.
characters.contradictions: Claims sobriety and discipline but lives a rough, itinerant life.
characters.values: Loyalty to Dravot, adherence to the Contrack, and brotherhood.
characters.continuity_facts: Has distinctive eyebrows and a moustache, travels with Dravot, referred to as 'Brother Peachey Carnehan'.

world_bible.name: British India & Native States
world_bible.description: A colonial landscape divided between British administrative zones and semi-autonomous Native States ruled by local princes.
world_bible.significance: Provides the backdrop of bureaucratic constraint and political intrigue that drives the protagonists to seek freedom elsewhere.

world_bible.name: Railway System
world_bible.description: A hierarchical transportation network with distinct classes (First, Second, Intermediate) reflecting social and economic status.
world_bible.significance: Facilitates the chance meeting of characters and symbolizes the rigid social order the protagonists wish to escape.

world_bible.name: Kafiristan
world_bible.description: An uncharted, mountainous region in the far northeast of Afghanistan, inhabited by heathen tribes and considered impassable by Englishmen.
world_bible.significance: The ultimate goal and testing ground for the protagonists' ambition, representing the unknown and the frontier of empire.

world_bible.name: The Contrack
world_bible.description: A strict personal agreement between Dravot and Carnehan forbidding alcohol and women, designed to maintain discipline and focus.
world_bible.significance: Establishes the brothers' code of conduct and foreshadows the challenges of maintaining order in an untamed land.

story_arcs.name: Ambition vs. Reality
story_arcs.description: The protagonists' grandiose dream of kingship clashes with the harsh, uncharted realities of Kafiristan and human limitations.

story_arcs.name: Brotherhood & Loyalty
story_arcs.description: The bond between Dravot and Carnehan is tested by their shared ambition and the strict rules of their Contrack.

story_arcs.name: Observer to Participant
story_arcs.description: The narrator shifts from a passive traveler and newspaperman to an active enabler of the quest, providing maps and knowledge.

sequences.name: The Train Encounter
sequences.description: The narrator meets Dravot and Carnehan on an Intermediate class train; they request a message delivery.

sequences.name: The Journey & Message
sequences.description: The narrator travels through Central India and the desert, delivering the coded message at Marwar Junction.

sequences.name: The Newspaper Office
sequences.description: The narrator settles into a stifling newspaper job, reflecting on colonial life and the pressures of the press.

sequences.name: The Return & The Plan
sequences.description: Dravot and Carnehan return to the office, reveal their plan to conquer Kafiristan, and request maps and books, setting the stage for the adventure.

narrative_constraints: First-person limited perspective restricts knowledge to the narrator's experiences and observations. The story is set in a specific historical colonial context, requiring accurate period-appropriate details and attitudes. The narrative ends on a preparatory note, focusing on setup and character motivation rather than the adventure itself.
success_definition: The story successfully establishes the characters' motivations, the historical setting, and the central quest, leaving the reader eager to see if their audacious plan will succeed or fail.
